messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High SRV lookup error rate detected in us-west-2b for service-discovery (consul -> coreDNS) — 5m error rate 6.8% (threshold 1%). Pager triggered. thread:2003456789

sara_oncall: acked. I'm on it, starting triage. Can someone grab logs from the consul agents in us-west-2b?

maya_devex: on it. hitting consul http endpoints now, pulling health and kv metrics. quick check: `consul members` returns nodes, but a few are in state: suspect.

jim_neteng: saw a spike in intra-AZ packet drops around 03:12 UTC from the cloud provider (AZ fabric telemetry). Could be noisy links causing UDP timeouts to coreDNS. Confirming with cloud support now.

oliver_platform: booking a short mitigation window. If this is the AZ fabric, we should fail traffic for service-discovery lookups off AZ2 to avoid tail latency. Suggest flip route preference for SRV lookups to us-west-2a/c for 15m while we stabilize.

sara_oncall: before we route, can we validate impact surface? lin_csm, any active customers flagged?

lin_csm: Customer telemetry shows 3 customers with increased 5xx errors for auth-service in us-west-2b (api gateway logs). Percent of requests failing due to backend connection issues ~3.8% overall, concentrated on hosts in that AZ. Customers notified via status page about degraded performance in us-west-2 (we included a note to say we're investigating).

maya_devex: digging into coreDNS logs — I'm seeing repeated UDP timeouts and truncated responses when consul attempts SRV queries. Example snippet:```
[coreDNS] 2026-03-15T03:13:21Z ERROR lookup.go:92 "dns: read udp 10.2.5.12:53: i/o timeout" for query _auth._tcp.service.local
```
Also consul logs show backoff on SRV queries.

jim_neteng: cloud support confirmed a partial network fabric malfunction in us-west-2b causing transient packet loss between hypervisors and the AZ egress routers. They've opened a ticket and are doing a fabric switchover. ETA unknown but they're prioritizing control plane.

oliver_platform: mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily prefer other AZs for SRV resolution via router policy change (smart-router config). 2) Increase consul query retries/timeout in the short term. 3) Flush coredns caches to avoid returning stale NODATA that clients interpret as hard failures. 4) Notify oncall for extended followup if cloud doesn't stabilize.

sara_oncall: implement steps 1 and 3. I can patch the router policy now. Maya, can you push a DNS cache flush to coreDNS pods?

maya_devex: pushing flush script to coreDNS in us-west-2b now:```
kubectl -n kube-system exec deploy/coredns -- /bin/sh -c "kill -HUP 1" || for p in $(kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o name); do kubectl -n kube-system exec $p -- coredns-control cache flush; done
```
Done — flushed caches at 03:22 UTC.

oliver_platform: router policy toggled at 03:23 UTC: SRV-pref = prefer (us-west-2a, us-west-2c) over us-west-2b for 10m. Also bumped consul client retry from 2 -> 4 and timeout from 2s -> 5s via a quick rollout to consul agents (can revert later).

incident-bot: Change recorded: route-policy/srv-pref updated by oliver_platform at 2003457300.

sara_oncall: monitoring shows error rate dropping. 1m error now 1.4%, 5m 2.6% and trending down. Keep rolling.

jim_neteng: cloud reported completion of fabric maintenance on the affected spine switches at 03:35 UTC — they believe root cause was a software bug causing egress packet drops for a subset of tenant traffic. They rolled a fix and are validating.

maya_devex: after cache flush and routing change, coreDNS logs show normal response times and fewer timeouts. Sample:```
[coreDNS] 2026-03-15T03:29:10Z INFO lookup.go:12 "query _auth._tcp.service.local -> 200ms"
```

lin_csm: Customer impact update: error windows were between 03:10–03:28 UTC, affecting roughly 3.8% of requests in us-west-2b for those customers. Post-mitigation, error rates returned to baseline. Communicating update to affected customer POCs.

oliver_platform: rolling back the consul retry bump to original values at 03:45 UTC — we want to revert any increased load on consul we introduced. Router policy will stay in prefer mode until we're +1h stable.

sara_oncall: agree. I'll keep watches for 1 hour, then plan to revert the route pref if nothing else appears. Prep a follow-up doc for post-incident.

raj_nightoncall: @sara_oncall I'm taking the 04:30–08:30 UTC window. Can you handoff any open actions?

sara_oncall: handing off: 1) monitor SRV error rate in us-west-2b for next 60m; threshold: 1% 5m. 2) if error rate goes above 1.5% for 5m, re-enable router pref and escalate to neteng. 3) ensure cloud support incident ID 987654 is tracked. I've added todos in the incident runbook.

raj_nightoncall: ack. I've subscribed to the alerts and pulled the runbook. I'll update if anything flares.

incident-bot: Note: on-call handoff recorded — from sara_oncall to raj_nightoncall at 2003460000.

maya_devex: postmortem checklist item: collect coreDNS and consul metrics + packet captures from hosts in us-west-2b between 03:05–03:40 UTC and attach to the ticket. I'll start packaging the logs.

oliver_platform: customer impact summary for postmortem: brief outage window (03:10–03:28 UTC), ~3.8% request failures for subset of customers in west region, root cause = AZ fabric packet loss leading to UDP timeouts for SRV queries. Mitigations: cache flush, route pref, consul retry bump (temporary). Action items: add an automatic fallback policy for SRV queries to prefer TCP for lookups > X ms, and add late-stage routing circuit to avoid single-AZ dependency for service-discovery.

lin_csm: I'm prepping an update to customers and the status page w/estimated root cause and mitigation. ETA 15m.

sara_oncall: thanks everyone — handing the channel to @raj_nightoncall for overnight monitoring. I'll draft the incident stub and timeline now. :white_check_mark:

raj_nightoncall: taking over.
